body_markdown:
Kevin Carroll


- [How-to Articles](https://testrigor.com/blog/category/how-to-articles/)


**Weekly Newsletter**
Receive weekly testRigor newsletters packed with insights on test automation, codeless testing, and the latest advancements in AI.


You can connect GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code to testRigor so that Copilot can help you create, run, troubleshoot, and maintain automated tests.


You do **not** need programming experience or previous command-line experience to complete this setup.


This guide walks through setting up the testRigor CLI, MCP server, and testRigor Skills with GitHub Copilot built into Visual Studio Code on Windows.


## How it Works:


GitHub Copilot + testRigor


There are four important pieces in this setup. They work together, but each has a different job.


🤖


GitHub Copilot


Your AI coding agent


Copilot works inside VS Code and lets you describe what you want to accomplish in normal language.


⌨️


testRigor CLI


Command-line access


Allows testRigor operations to be performed from the command line instead of only through the web interface.


🔗


MCP


Connect Copilot to testRigor


Allows Copilot in VS Code to communicate directly with testRigor and use the tools provided by the testRigor MCP server.


🧠


testRigor Skills


Teach Copilot testRigor


Give Copilot testRigor-specific instructions for writing tests, using the CLI, and following testRigor workflows.


**The complete setup:** Prepare VS Code → Install the testRigor CLI → Add the testRigor Skills → Connect testRigor through MCP → Enable the MCP tools → Start working.


## Prepare:


Get VS Code and GitHub Copilot Ready


### Step 1 · Open Visual Studio Code


Open **Visual Studio Code** .


Make sure GitHub Copilot is available in VS Code.


Look for the **GitHub Copilot icon** in the VS Code interface.


If Copilot asks you to sign in or authorize access, follow the prompts and sign in with the GitHub account associated with your Copilot access.


Screenshot needed


VS Code showing the GitHub Copilot icon and Copilot Chat panel.


After signing in, open the Copilot Chat panel.


Depending on your GitHub account, you may be using Copilot Free or another Copilot plan. The setup in this guide does not depend on the plan name displayed in the video.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when GitHub Copilot Chat is available inside VS Code.


### Step 2 · Open PowerShell


We will use PowerShell to install the testRigor command-line tool.


Click the Windows **Start** button and search for:


```text
PowerShell
```


Open PowerShell.


You should see something similar to:


```text
PS C:\Users\YourName>
```


Your actual Windows username will appear instead of` YourName` .


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when PowerShell is open and you see a line beginning with` PS` .


### Step 3 · Check Node.js


The testRigor CLI requires Node.js version 18 or newer.


Check whether Node.js is already installed:


```text
node --version
```


Then check npm:


```text
npm --version
```


If both commands return version numbers, continue.


If Node.js is not installed, download the current **LTS** version for Windows from the official[Node.js website](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) .


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when both` node --version` and` npm --version` return version numbers.


## Install:


Add the testRigor CLI


### Step 4 · Install the testRigor CLI


In PowerShell, run:


```text
npm install -g @testrigor/testrigor-cli
```


npm will download and install the testRigor CLI and its required packages.


When the normal PowerShell prompt returns, verify the installation:


```text
testrigor --version
```


You should see a testRigor CLI version number.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when` testrigor --version` returns a version number.


**npm says that running scripts is disabled** Troubleshooting help


Try:


```text
npm.cmd --version
```


If that returns a version number, use:


```text
npm.cmd install -g @testrigor/testrigor-cli
```


instead of the normal` npm` command.


## Connect:


Create Your testRigor Authentication Token


### Step 5 · Generate a testRigor Personal Authentication Token


The CLI and MCP connection need permission to communicate with your testRigor account.


testRigor provides this through a **Personal Authentication Token** , or **PAT** .


In testRigor:


1. Click your username in the upper-right corner.
2. Select **API Tokens** .
3. Click **Generate New Token** .
4. Give the token a clear name, such as` VS Code MCP` .
5. Choose an expiration that follows your organization’s security policy.
6. Generate the token.
7. Copy it.


Screenshot needed


testRigor API Tokens page showing Generate New Token.


**Keep this token available.** You will use it to authenticate the testRigor CLI and configure the MCP server.


**Treat the PAT like a password.** Do not expose it in screenshots, public documentation, chat messages, or source-control repositories.


### Step 6 · Authenticate the testRigor CLI


Return to PowerShell and run:


```text
testrigor authenticate
```


The CLI will ask for your testRigor Personal Authentication Token.


Paste the token and press **Enter** .


The CLI should confirm that authentication has been saved.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when the CLI confirms that authentication was saved.


## Add the Skills:


Teach GitHub Copilot How to Work with testRigor


### Step 7 · Download the testRigor Skills


testRigor Skills are reusable instruction packages that give Copilot additional guidance about how to work with testRigor.


🔁


testrigor-dev-loop


The end-to-end workflow


Helps Copilot build, run, inspect, fix, and run tests again as part of an iterative development loop.


✍️


testrigor-write-tests


Writing testRigor tests


Helps Copilot write and edit testRigor tests, reusable rules, and other testRigor test content.


⌨️


testrigor-cli


Using the CLI


Helps Copilot understand and use testRigor command-line functionality correctly.


Open the[testRigor Skills repository on GitHub](https://github.com/TestRigor/skills) .


Click the **Code** dropdown and select **Download ZIP** .


Screenshot needed


GitHub testRigor Skills repository with the Download ZIP option visible.


After the ZIP file downloads, open your **Downloads** folder.


### Step 8 · Create Copilot’s Personal Skills Folder


GitHub Copilot can discover personal Skills stored in your Windows user profile.


Navigate to:


```text
C:\Users\YourName\.copilot
```


Replace` YourName` with your actual Windows username.


Inside the` .copilot` folder, create a new folder named:


```text
skills
```


Your final path should look similar to:


```text
C:\Users\YourName\.copilot\skills
```


Screenshot needed


Windows File Explorer showing the .copilot\\skills directory.


### Step 9 · Copy the testRigor Skills


Extract the downloaded testRigor Skills ZIP file.


Inside the extracted repository, locate the three testRigor Skill folders:


```text
testrigor-cli
testrigor-dev-loop
testrigor-write-tests
```


Copy those three folders directly into:


```text
C:\Users\YourName\.copilot\skills
```


Each Skill must remain in its own folder.


The resulting structure should look similar to:


```text
.copilot
└── skills
├── testrigor-cli
├── testrigor-dev-loop
└── testrigor-write-tests
```


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when the three testRigor Skill folders are directly inside` .copilot\\skills` .


### Step 10 · Confirm the Skills in VS Code


Return to VS Code.


Open the Copilot customization settings using the **gear** icon and select **Skills** .


You should see the three testRigor Skills:


```text
testrigor-cli
testrigor-dev-loop
testrigor-write-tests
```


Screenshot needed


VS Code Skills view showing the three installed testRigor Skills.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when the three testRigor Skills are visible in VS Code.


## Add MCP:


Connect GitHub Copilot Directly to testRigor


### Step 11 · Open the Project in VS Code


The video configures testRigor MCP at the **workspace level** . This means the MCP configuration belongs to the particular project folder you open in VS Code.


Open the folder where you want to use testRigor with GitHub Copilot.


For example, the video uses a project folder containing testRigor UI scripts.


### Step 12 · Create the VS Code MCP Configuration


In the root of your project, create a folder named exactly:


```text
.vscode
```


**Include the period at the beginning.**


Inside the` .vscode` folder, create a new file named:


```text
mcp.json
```


Your project structure should now look similar to:


```text
your-project
└── .vscode
└── mcp.json
```


Screenshot needed


VS Code Explorer showing .vscode/mcp.json inside the project.


### Step 13 · Add the testRigor MCP Server


Open` .vscode/mcp.json` and paste:


```text
{
"servers": {
"testrigor": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://api2.testrigor.com/api/v1/mcp",
"headers": {
"personal-access-token": "YOUR_TESTRIGOR_PAT"
}
}
}
}
```


Replace:


```text
YOUR_TESTRIGOR_PAT
```


with the Personal Authentication Token you generated earlier.


Do **not** leave the placeholder text in the configuration.


Save the file. On Windows, you can press:


```text
Ctrl + S
```


Screenshot needed


VS Code showing the completed mcp.json configuration. Blur or replace the real PAT before publishing the screenshot.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when the file has been saved successfully.


### Step 14 · Confirm testRigor Appears in MCP Servers


Open the Copilot customization settings using the **gear** icon and go to **MCP Servers** .


You should now see **testRigor** listed.


Screenshot needed


VS Code MCP Servers view showing testRigor.


At this point, the server has been configured. Next, make sure its tools are enabled for Copilot Agent mode.


### Step 15 · Enable the testRigor MCP Tools


Open Copilot Chat and make sure you are using **Agent** mode.


Open the chat’s **More Actions** menu and select the option to configure tools.


Find **testRigor** in the available tools.


Make sure the checkbox for the testRigor MCP server is enabled.


You can expand it to see the individual tools provided by the server.


Screenshot needed


Copilot Agent mode tool configuration showing testRigor MCP enabled.


**✓ Checkpoint** — Continue when testRigor is enabled in the Agent tools list.


### Step 16 · Test the MCP Connection


Now give Copilot a simple read-only request.


For example:


```text
Which MCP servers do you have access to?
```


Copilot should recognize the testRigor MCP server.


You can also try a testRigor-specific request:


```text
List the testRigor test suites I have access to.
```


Copilot should use the testRigor MCP tools to retrieve the suites available to your testRigor user.


If you return to **MCP Servers** , VS Code may display testRigor as running after the MCP connection has been used.


Screenshot needed


VS Code showing testRigor MCP with a running or connected status indicator.


**✓ Checkpoint** — If Copilot can access testRigor through MCP, the connection is working.


## Start Working:


Use GitHub Copilot with testRigor


At this point, GitHub Copilot has the three pieces it needs for the complete testRigor integration:


✓ testRigor CLI


Installed and authenticated with your testRigor account.


✓ testRigor MCP


Copilot can communicate directly with testRigor using MCP tools.


✓ testRigor Skills


Copilot has testRigor-specific guidance available when relevant.


You can now use Copilot Agent mode and describe what you want to do in normal English.


For example:


```text
Help me write a testRigor test that logs in and verifies that the dashboard appears.
```


Or:


```text
Run my testRigor tests and help me troubleshoot the failures.
```


Or:


```text
List my test suites and show me the test cases in the suite named Regression.
```


## Troubleshooting:


If Something Doesn’t Look Right


If everything is working, you do not need to read the sections below. Open only the problem that matches what you are seeing.


**The testRigor Skills do not appear in VS Code** Troubleshooting help


Check that the three Skill folders are located directly inside:


```text
C:\Users\YourName\.copilot\skills
```


You should have:


```text
.copilot
└── skills
├── testrigor-cli
├── testrigor-dev-loop
└── testrigor-write-tests
```


Do not leave them nested inside an additional downloaded repository folder such as` skills-main` .


If necessary, restart VS Code after moving the folders.


**testRigor does not appear under MCP Servers** Troubleshooting help


Make sure the file is located at:


```text
your-project\.vscode\mcp.json
```


Check that the VS Code configuration uses:


```text
"servers"
```


as the top-level property.


Also verify that the server contains:


```text
"type": "http"
```


and that the URL is` https://api2.testrigor.com/api/v1/mcp` .


**testRigor appears but Copilot does not use its tools** Troubleshooting help


First, make sure Copilot Chat is in **Agent** mode.


Then open the tools configuration from the chat’s More Actions menu.


Find testRigor and confirm that it is enabled.


MCP tools must be available to Agent mode before Copilot can invoke them.


**MCP authentication fails** Troubleshooting help


Check whether:


- The PAT was copied completely.
- The PAT has expired or been revoked.
- The header is named` personal-access-token` .
- The testRigor user associated with the token still has access.
- A company firewall or network policy could be blocking the MCP connection.


**MCP does not bypass testRigor permissions.**


**Copilot can connect but cannot access my test suite** Troubleshooting help


Sign in to the testRigor web application as the user who created the PAT.


Try to open the same test suite there.


If that user cannot access the suite in testRigor, Copilot will not gain additional access through MCP.
